graph-model.title: Several graphs, each serving a different question
graph-model.summary: The inspected implementation contains explicit navigation nodes and links, TypeScript project references and a Three.js scene hierarchy. Review code branches and joins; asset validators encode dependency relationships. These are distinct representations.

entries.title: Review join

graph-build.summary: The client references shared; the server references shared and client. With arrows meaning prerequisite to consumer, the diagram shows all three relationships. Typecheck uses TypeScript build mode.

graph-nav.title: Bots search a navigation graph within a budget
graph-nav.summary: Sampled places become navigation nodes. Neighbor links are checked against the physics world. A* returns a route with an explicit completion flag and a default 4,000-expansion limit.

entries.title: Node and route interfaces
entries.explanation: Nodes carry coordinates and neighbor indices. route returns points plus complete.

entries.title: A* search and expansion budget
entries.explanation: The default cap is 4,000 expansions. findPath at line 117 prioritizes cost plus heuristic and can return a partial path.

entries.title: Walkable neighbor connections
entries.explanation: Neighbor links are added in both directions only after edge walkability checks. The initial wander pool uses the largest connected component.

entries.title: Selected graph goal
entries.explanation: World coordinates are mapped to suitable graph nodes; completion refers to reaching the chosen graph goal.

entries.title: Local invalidation after prop changes
entries.explanation: A per-world overlay rechecks touched nodes and edges. The wander pool is filtered from the original pool rather than recomputing the largest component on each invalidation.

entries.title: Partial-route handling
entries.explanation: Steering distinguishes a partial route from arrival and can search again.

graph-nav.limit: The graph samples navigable positions and uses its own movement costs. It does not establish the shortest route through every possible real-world position. Partial results and search limits are explicit. No current gameplay tests were rerun for this source review.

graph-scene.title: A scene tree makes connected parts inherit movement
graph-scene.summary: The partner view creates nested Three.js groups. The shoulder owns arm, hand and blade; body owns shoulder; figure owns body; the outer group owns figure.

entries.title: Groups are created
entries.explanation: The view constructs group, figure, body and shoulder objects.

entries.title: Children are attached to parents
entries.explanation: The add calls establish the nested scene hierarchy.

entries.title: Shoulder animation
entries.explanation: Shoulder rotation is changed by animation; descendants inherit the transform through their parent relationship.

graph-assets.title: Changed inputs invalidate generated lighting
graph-assets.summary: The market neon installer checks source fingerprints, scene metadata and texture bytes. Runtime code checks layout and scene compatibility before accepting a lighting bake.

entries.title: Check source-file versions
entries.explanation: Source files must exist inside the checkout and match their recorded fingerprints. Changed sources are rejected with instructions to re-export and rebake.

entries.title: Check manifest and texture
entries.explanation: Expected scene fields must agree; texture bytes are checked against the recorded fingerprint at line 123.

entries.title: Check runtime compatibility
entries.explanation: The current layout and calculated scene fingerprints must match the stored bake metadata.

graph-assets.limit: The relationships are encoded by contracts and fingerprints; this is not evidence of a dedicated knowledge-graph database. Matching versions do not prove visual quality or that a prepared cloud job successfully ran.

graph-feedback.title: The column correction and the documented repair cycle
graph-feedback.summary: Sampled column records show observation, investigation, correction and checks. Separately, the handoff protocol documents another repair round when checks fail or serious findings remain.
graph-feedback.card: Hidden column detail prompted a correction, ray-based checks, and visual review.

entries.title: Supporting project artifact
entries.explanation: The first proposed Palace column grooves were behind flat panels and could not be seen. Review rejected them. A raycast test checks the raised face and recessed groove differ by more than seven centimetres; the recorded two-file run passed 23 checks.
